basics.name: John Walley
basics.label: Senior Software Engineer | React, TypeScript & Data Visualisation
basics.summary: Senior software engineer with 20+ years of experience building analytical, data-intensive web applications for engineering, scientific and financial users, including real-time visualisations over large datasets. Strong React, TypeScript and JavaScript expertise, with experience designing frontend architectures, reusable component APIs, real-time data flows and performance-sensitive browser interactions. Comfortable working directly with technical users, often as the sole engineer, to understand complex workflows and turn them into effective software. Experienced in setting engineering direction, mentoring developers, and taking solutions from initial design through production delivery. Strong mathematical and scientific-computing background, with degrees from Cambridge and Oxford and earlier roles in high-performance and scientific computing.

work.name: Cambridge Intelligence
work.summary: Working across browser-based graph, timeline and geospatial visualisation SDKs, React applications, developer experience and customer-facing technical platforms.
highlights: Designed frontend architectures and developer-facing APIs for interactive visualisations operating over large, complex datasets.

Built and optimised browser interactions involving large stateful data models and performance-sensitive rendering across Canvas and WebGL pipelines; the SDKs support visualisations of 40,000+ items at interactive frame rates.
Contributed to technical and product decisions across rendering, animation, state management, API design, usability and developer experience.

Lead the design and build of a unified documentation, examples and showcase website for four SDK products, including its React example gallery, consolidating separate sites and tooling into a single codebase and delivery pipeline; defined the ownership, review and release workflows that let product and website development proceed in parallel.

Chair the Website Team's Technical Strategy Group, setting priorities across AI-assisted engineering, testing architecture, accessibility and component standardisation; personally drive the team's AI-assisted engineering priority and support development of its automated testing approach.
Mentor a graduate developer through regular 1:1s, pairing, career guidance and development-goal setting.

work.name: Mulberry House Software
work.summary: Independent consultancy building React applications, interactive visualisation systems, data-driven analytical software and open-source developer tools. Sole engineer on client engagements, responsible for understanding user needs, architecture, backend and API integration, implementation and production delivery.
highlights: Created and maintained [Allotment](https://allotment.mulberryhousesoftware.com/), an open-source React split-pane layout component with over 10 million npm downloads.

Designed and delivered data visualisation software for pensions technology company [Financial Canvas](https://www.financialcanvas.co.uk/), enabling pension scheme managers to explore data and inform investment decisions.

Created [Pennant](https://github.com/vegaprotocol/pennant), an open-source Canvas-based financial charting library that was used in production by the Vega decentralised trading network, supporting candlesticks, depth charts, panning, zooming and crosshair interactions.
Designed Pennant's client-side real-time data flow using WebSockets, integrating streaming market data from backend APIs with responsive, high-performance visualisations.
Designed reusable APIs and abstractions for complex interactive interfaces, balancing flexibility, performance and developer usability.
Developed an interactive floor-planning application for home-renovation startup [Reno](https://www.renovatewithreno.co.uk/).

Owned projects from requirements and initial product design through architecture, implementation, deployment and support, working directly with clients to understand workflows and make technical and product decisions.

work.name: Redgate
work.position: Software Developer, then Trainee Product Manager
work.summary: Developed C#/.NET tooling for SQL Server database deployment before moving into product management for an acquired database deployment product.
highlights: Developed developer-facing features to improve the reliability and usability of SQL Server database deployment within CI/CD pipelines.
Used customer research and in-product analytics to understand user workflows and prioritise product and UX improvements that increased adoption.

work.name: SunGard
work.summary: Developed C#/.NET infrastructure for high-performance financial risk analytics.
highlights: Developed a tracing JIT compiler that enabled existing C# financial models to execute on GPUs without requiring the models to be rewritten.
Contributed to the scalable execution framework underpinning computationally intensive financial risk calculations.

work.name: Earlier Career
work.summary: Engineering and research roles in high-performance computing, scientific computing and financial systems.
highlights: High Performance Computing Developer at [Fidelity](https://www.fidelity.co.uk/), building computationally intensive systems for financial services.
Application Engineer at [MathWorks](https://www.mathworks.com/), serving as UK technical contact for parallel computing tools and helping developers solve complex computational problems.

Research Scientist at [QinetiQ](https://www.qinetiq.com/), developing tracking and estimation algorithms including Kalman filtering and multi-target tracking for multi-sensor fusion and defence systems.
Studied mathematical modelling, numerical linear algebra, numerical optimisation and distributed computing for computational finance.
Dissertation on the numerical solution of magnetic fluid flow.
